description.text:
The promos of Japan's PCG years: 154 cards, 001/PCG-P to 154/PCG-P, released from February 2004 to July 2006. They began soon after Undone Seal, the last Japanese expansion with the ADV prefix, when the promo suffix changed from ADV-P to PCG-P.

Most came in a few big runs: Meiji Chocolate cards in 2004, 2005 and 2006, McDonald's promotions in 2005 and 2006, the attraction cards of the PokéPark 2005 theme park, and Battle Road prizes every season, from participation cards to finals prizes such as the Holon Energy cards of autumn 2005. Others came with CoroCoro Comic, Shogakukan's elementary school magazines and Pokémon Wonderland, with the film Mew and the Wave Hero: Lucario and the video of Pikachu's Summer Festival, in official card files, deck cases and the Team Rocket Special Boxes, from the Official Pokémon Card Gym lotteries, for Pokémon Center openings, and in All Nippon Airways' Pika Summer Trip of 2006.

Katsura Tabata's Pokémon Card Laboratory was the prize for beating a researcher of the Pokémon Card Laboratory (PCL), the team that makes the game, at the Gym Leader & PCL Challenge corner of Battle Road Summer 2004. Players who beat PCL won it again at the 21st Next Generation World Hobby Fair in January and February 2005 and at Battle Road Summer 2006, where the official report said few players managed it.

Once during each player's turn, they may choose a Pokémon card from their hand, say its name and put it face down; the opponent then names one of its attacks. If they are right, the opponent draws a card; if not, the player draws one. The card then goes back to the hand.

description.text:
Mitsuhiro Arita's Rocket's Persian ex, in holofoil, was given to everyone who played in the Team Rocket One Day Battle, a side event at Battle Road Spring 2005. Its double battles used 60-card decks holding at least seven cards from the Team Rocket half decks W -black- and W -silver- or the expansion ロケット団の逆襲 (Team Rocket Returns in English). Three wins in a row earned a set of holo basic Energies (055 to 060/PCG-P). The non-holo copy, 036/PCG-P, came first, at the 21st Next Generation World Hobby Fair in early 2005.

Battle Road Spring 2005 held nine tournaments in seven cities from 13 March 2005, open to players who had applied in advance. The junior and senior league winners of each went to the 2005 World Championships in the United States. The Kyushu tournament, called off on 20 March by an earthquake, was finished on 8 May.
